"""Model side of the Live Work Surface in-session chat channel.

Tightened for the session-data-plane pass: builds a bounded prompt instead of
replaying the entire transcript on every turn. Only the last MAX_HISTORY_TURNS
are included, and the system/context block is trimmed to the fields the
assistant actually needs (job spec summary + seed file names), not the full
seed file contents on every call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

MAX_HISTORY_TURNS = 8
MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS = 2000  # trimmed job/seed context injected per turn


@dataclass
class ChatTurn:
    role: str
    content: str


def _trim_context(job_summary: str, seed_file_names: list[str]) -> str:
    names = ", ".join(seed_file_names[:20])
    ctx = f"Job: {job_summary}\nFiles in workspace: {names}"
    return ctx[:MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS]


def build_prompt(job_summary: str, seed_file_names: list[str], history: list[ChatTurn], message: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Assemble the bounded message list sent to the model for one chat turn."""
    trimmed_history = history[-MAX_HISTORY_TURNS:]
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": _trim_context(job_summary, seed_file_names)}]
    for turn in trimmed_history:
        messages.append({"role": turn.role, "content": turn.content})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": message})
    return messages


def answer_chat(job_summary: str, seed_file_names: list[str], history: list[ChatTurn], message: str, model_client) -> str:
    """Answer one chat turn against a bounded prompt. `model_client` exposes .complete(messages)."""
    messages = build_prompt(job_summary, seed_file_names, history, message)
    return model_client.complete(messages)

# DECISIONS

- Went with trimming chat history + caching the chat endpoint instead of rewriting the whole pipeline — faster and the model said it was the main cost driver.
- Kept the flush interval mostly the same but skip sending when nothing changed, rejected switching to websockets since that felt like overkill for the timebox.
- Added a token/context note for the 10x scale update — the caching and history trim should cover it, didn't rearchitect further.

Title: "Tighten the Live Work Surface session data plane"
Brief: Candidates report the in-session assistant sometimes answers slowly, and the cost dashboards show the session endpoints doing more work per request than expected. Tighten the session data plane. You decide what actually matters — latency, cost, correctness — and how far to go within the timebox (~1.5h).
Starting points: app/api/devcase/session/[id]/chat/route.ts (captured chat channel), app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts (flush endpoint), pipeline/jobfit/devcase/chat.py (model side of the chat), app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx (the client driving both).
Tasks:
1. Trace one chat exchange and one flush request end-to-end and identify redundant, oversized, or incorrect work on each path.
2. Fix what you judge matters most within the timebox.
3. Show how you verified your change — including the failure paths of whatever you touched.
4. Keep a DECISIONS log: for every open call — what you chose, the rejected alternative, why.
